newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spot mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spot mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Thursday, with market sentiment cautious on news that Beijing would gradually drive state banks out of the market, traders said.

But the annual rate for the most active seven-day contract bucked the trend and rose to 12.05 percent from 11.00 percent on Wednesday with institutions borrowing money on the repo market for bidding on a new domestic A share issue on Friday.
Combined volume rose sharply to 8.52 million lots from 3.42 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
The sharp rise in the volume today was mainly due to active trading in the seven-day contract, traders said.

Traders said officials from the People's Bank of China at a meeting in Beijing early this week told state banks to phase out trading on the state debt markets. The banks must not build new positions and existing positions must be gradually offset.
"The news will gradaully reduce trading volumes on the repo markets," said one trader. "But the rates are likely to go up in the longer run with money supply on the market decreasing."
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed having found support after losses in the past few trading days.
The most active three-year bond that matures in 1999 rose slightly to 103.28 yuan from 103 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose to 766,892 lots from a very thin 594,910 lots.
Traders said news that state banks would be gradually banned from T-bill secondary market had no big impact on the market today because no deadline had been set.
"Technical charts indicate the spot contract will continue to rise in the next few days but only slowly," one trader said.
